A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLaVA-KD, and their supplied pages are readable. v1 includes Appendix A and Tables A1–A4. v3 ends at the references despite citing an appendix for hyperparameters and detailed MobileVLM results. The main content supports reliable comparison, but those promised supplementary details are unavailable.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training-stage and distillation ablations, and qualitative examples, including detailed results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original evaluations and adds Qwen2.5 results, controlled distillation comparisons, MobileVLM experiments, and teacher-size studies.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, visual/response KL distillation, relation cosine loss, and DPT–SFT–DFT procedure remain unchanged. Additional backbone experiments test the existing framework. Corrections to student/teacher wording and loss notation clarify the procedure rather than establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both use LLaVA1.5-558k and LLaVA-mix-665k and evaluate VQAv2, GQA, VizWiz, ScienceQA, TextVQA, MME, MMB, MMBCN, POPE, and MMMU. Additional backbone and teacher configurations do not introduce different datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds LLaVADI and Qwen2.5 TinyLLaVA baselines to Table 1, FKL/RKL/JSD comparisons in Table 5, and controlled Mimic Distillation and Mimic-plus-Preference Distillation alternatives in Table 6. Table 1 drops BLIP-2, LLaVA-NeXT, MobileVLMv2, LLaVA-Phi, and MiniCPMv2. These substantially revise the evaluated comparison set.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Qwen2.5 configurations, 7B teachers, MobileVLM teacher/student configurations, and PT–SFT–DFT and DPT–DFT–DFT controls. Table 1 replaces its nine-benchmark average with seven- and ten-benchmark averages, although these aggregation schemes appeared elsewhere in v1. No changed hyperparameters for retained runs are established.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analysis through additional training-stage controls, alternative distillation losses and pipelines, MobileVLM transfer, and teacher-size sensitivity studies (Tables 2 and 5–8). Original component and token-target ablations retain their summary results. v1's qualitative cases and explicit training-efficiency comparison are absent from v3, while detailed appendix breakdowns are unavailable.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The additional experimental configurations do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Retained Qwen1.5 LLaVA-KD per-benchmark scores are unchanged, but substantial results are added: Qwen2.5-0.5B reaches 58.9 Avg10, MobileVLM improves from 48.8 to 53.4 under the proposed training recipe, and additional controls and teacher-size comparisons appear. These are newly reported configurations, not improvements over identical v1 settings. Changed headline averages also reflect different benchmark subsets.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same autoregressive, KL, self-correlation, and cosine-loss formulations. Replacing L_PT with L_reg in Equation 6 clarifies notation. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation appears; the teacher-capacity discussion is empirical interpretation.

C1.justification: The principal MDist/RDist and three-stage-training contributions remain. The introduction drops the explicit contribution claim that the 1B model surpasses BLIP2-13B and InstructBLIP-7B, instead emphasizing superiority over recent small MLLMs. This modestly redirects the headline comparative claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning teacher–student capacity mismatch, an alignment bottleneck explaining weaker transfer from larger teachers, preference distillation's hallucination/comprehension tradeoff, and DFT compensating for weaker pretraining. It also argues for the three-stage scheme's computational tradeoff. The existing shared-vocabulary limitation remains and is extended to discuss capacity matching.

D1.justification: v1 Section 4.1 specifies batch sizes 32/16, learning rates 1e-3/2e-5, one epoch per stage, AdamW, cosine scheduling, eight L40s GPUs, and 210/320 GPU-hour totals. v3 retains architecture, datasets, and loss weights but defers detailed settings to an absent appendix. This substantially reduces reproducibility information in the supplied document without establishing changed underlying settings. The code-availability promise is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of LLaVADI and references on distillation scaling, CLIP-KD, and f-divergence, alongside additional segmentation and grounding examples. These update specific comparisons and interpretations while retaining the overall related-work taxonomy and positioning around architectural simplicity and training optimization.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting. The standalone LLaVA-MoD discussion and visualization/exploration subsection disappear, while comparisons and limitations are reorganized within the expanded experimental narrative. These changes substantially revise exposition beyond merely inserting new results.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn without its radar panel, Figure 3 disappears, Table 1 gains sample-count and separate average columns, and Table 4 merges its two panels. New comparison tables replace and extend the earlier displays; v1's appendix tables are not present in the supplied v3.

improvement.justification: The added controls and comparisons in Tables 2 and 5–8 strengthen validation of the training scheme, alternative distillation choices, and transfer across model configurations. However, v3 no longer supplies v1's detailed training settings, full ablation breakdowns, or timing comparison, and its referenced appendix is missing. These empirical gains and reproducibility losses leave the net quality change uncertain from the supplied PDFs.
